In the North-West Frontier Province, under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a volunteer organization named ‘Khudai Khidmatgar’ was established. They were also known as the ‘Red Shirts’. The ‘Red Shirts’ raised the slogan of national unity among the Pathans, organized a movement against British colonialism for independence, and demanded improvement in the condition of working people. It is noteworthy that when Muslims in other provinces were keeping themselves away from the Satyagraha movement, the Muslims of the North-West Frontier Province, under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar, played an important role in the Civil Disobedience Movement.

The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was concluded on 5 March, 1931. According to this pact- (i) Under Gandhi’s leadership, the Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement. (ii) Orders were issued to release political prisoners against whom there was no allegation of violence. (iii) The right to stage peaceful dharnas at foreign cloth shops and liquor shops was granted. (iv) In coastal regions, permission was given to make salt without paying the salt tax. (v) The Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference; however, this pact disappointed the public because it did not include the public demand that Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru should not be hanged.

stem: Who played an important role in the signing of Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
expl: Viceroy Irwin released Gandhi from jail on 26 January, 1931 to create an atmosphere of harmony in the country. Due to the efforts of Tej Bahadur Sapru, V.S. Srinivasa Sastri, and M.R. Jayakar, talks between Mahatma Gandhi and Irwin began in Delhi in February, 1931. On 5 March, 1931, an agreement was reached between them, which came to be known as the Gandhi–Irwin Pact. In this context, Sarojini Naidu described Gandhi and Irwin as “two Mahatmas”.
